reviewed_by: Claude Code, at the operator's request: a provider goal should wait for its working subagents instead of running turns that poll them
reason: After a provider goal turn completed, _continue_running_goal_after_turn started the next goal turn even while the goal's subagents were still working, so the parent ran full-context turns that only polled them (live Core: 321 wait_subagents and 291 list_subagents calls in 3 days). It now settles the goal's active time and returns when has_working_subagents is true, as the harness path and the idle reconciler already do; the subagent report delivery path (deliver_pending -> _continue_goal) resumes the goal once every subagent has finished. Goals with no working subagents continue as before. Selected: the subagent and subagent-lifecycle suites (new regression test: a running provider goal with two working subagents starts no continuation after its turn, and continues exactly once when both finish together), the goal suites, the goal-continuation settings test, the provider stream tests that stub the continuation, and test_chat.py for the changed module.
exclusions: Harness goal continuation is unchanged and its suites are not selected. No UI, settings or operator-visible control changes, so no browser, settings-assistant or LAN Core validation applies; the behaviour is covered by the real ChatService with a scripted provider.
